messages:
kevin: Heads up — saw a dedicated tenant hit its reserved throughput then start pulling from the shared pool. Caused a latency spike for others. Anyone digging into quota enforcement?
olivia: Which tenant? any SLAs affected?
sanjay: Tenant ID t-8792. They were at ~480rps on a 500rps reserved config, then they spiked to 900 for ~40s and we let them borrow from shared burst capacity.
maria: That borrowing should be capped by the tenant isolation limit (per-pool limit). Did isolation limit kick in? logs?
kevin: Logs show we allowed fallback because their per-org key still had burst tokens in the shared bucket. No hard throttle at the reserved boundary.
jess: That's by design for smooth degradation but agreed we need guardrails. We don't want a single dedicated tenant to stomp shared throughput.
aj: Quick context: current algorithm = reserved_quota hard guarantee; after that we allow borrowing from shared_burst_token_bucket (window=60s, tokens=1000). Isolation limit is 75% of pool QPS for any single tenant but it seems that check runs after token assignment.
olivia: So ordering bug: token bucket assignment before isolation check. We should flip checks: isolation first, then tokens. Small PR?
sanjay: Also need per-key vs per-org nuance — some customers use multiple keys. If we check per-key limits only, they can multiplex keys to exceed tenant hard limit.
maria: We already have per-org aggregation in metrics but enforcement path uses per-key struct. Patch should aggregate incoming tokens to org-level before enforcement.
kevin: Suggestion: enforce these invariants in the serving path (fast path) not in async quota daemon. If we wait for async correction, too late.
aj: Agree. Proposed change:
```yaml
quota_enforcement_order:
  - check_tenant_isolation
  - check_reserved_quota
  - check_shared_burst_tokens
  - check_per_key_rate
burst_window_seconds: 60
burst_tokens_per_pool: 1000
isolation_threshold_percent: 70
```
maria: That config looks reasonable. Also add a circuit-breaker that fails fast when pool utilization > 95% to avoid tail latency cascades.
jess: Devex: we should expose a Console metric that shows "current borrowed rps" per-tenant and per-pool and a flag showing which enforcement rule rejected a request.
olivia: UX: show a tooltip on tenant page: "Reserved throughput is guaranteed; burst access is opportunistic and subject to tenant isolation." Might reduce support noise.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: patch/eng/2785 -> quota-ordering-fix ( staging )
kevin: Nice, also add an alert: when any tenant borrows > 50% of shared pool for >30s, page oncall.
sanjay: I'll own the PR. Plan: aggregate per-key->per-org upstream, change ordering, add fast-path isolation check, write unit tests for token races, update metrics, then roll to staging.
maria: Can we do a canary rollout by tenant ID slicing? e.g., enable new ordering only for tenants with flag enable_quota_v2 on their org profile.
aj: Yeah we have rollout flags already. We'll use targetted rollout + telemetry to compare dropped request rate and tail-latency.
jess: Also add a tiny Console card showing "quota mode" (legacy vs v2) for each org so support can see who is on the new path.
kevin: Thanks. Sanjay, please include a short runbook entry: steps to revert and how to clear borrowed tokens for a noisy tenant without restart.
sanjay: Will do. ETA for PR review today, staging deploy tonight.
kevin: :thumbsup: will follow up on alerts and support messaging.
deploy-bot: deploy success: patch/eng/2785 -> staging (   1782043800 )
kevin: Staging logs look good; isolation check now rejects borrow attempts when pool is at 80% and tenant tries to exceed 70% of pool. Moving to canary tomorrow.
olivia: Great work, thanks everyone! :party_parrot:
